description: Step 2 of the extern door collapse. The proposal assumed dlsym alone could find runtime exports once the host binary exported its symbols dynamically. Measured: a runtime export nothing references (fz_aot_setup) is absent from the compiler binary on macOS, so the linker drops unreferenced exports before any dynamic-table question arises; the compiler's two hand-maintained address tables were the references keeping the symbols alive. The by-construction replacement: the runtime crate owns one RUNTIME_EXPORTS table (runtime/src/exports.rs) built by a macro from the export identifiers, so a row's name and address cannot disagree; runtime/src/export_test.rs holds it complete in both directions, including the macro-generated arithmetic and comparison exports. fz_extern_symbol_addr consults it before the loaded image, so it is the one resolver on every door. Deleted: runtime_symbol_addrs and register_runtime_symbols' production rows (src/ir_codegen/backend.rs), the interpreter's name->address match and its 60-name use list (src/ir_interp/extern_call.rs), every_declared_runtime_symbol_is_reachable_from_compiled_code. No linker flags, no platform-specific proof needed. Alternative if a zero-table shape is wanted later: linkme distributed_slice registration at each definition site, at the cost of a dependency and linker-section GC caveats.
title: Runtime owns its export table; delete the JIT registry and the interpreter address book
